issue: Tip overgeneralizes: 'χθες + past = one finished event' is false as a rule — χθες combines freely with the imperfect (χθες έβρεχε όλη μέρα). Misleads learners into thinking χθες forces the aorist.

fix.grammar: One finished event takes the simple past: χθες αγόρασα (chthes agórasa = yesterday I bought).

issue: Romanization missing accent: πώς is romanized 'pos' — accent position is phonemic and must be shown (pós).

fix.grammar: περνάω = spend time: Πώς πέρασες; (pós pérases = how was it / did you have fun?)

issue: Tip's worked example has an English translation in parentheses instead of the required romanization (τραγουδούσε όταν μαγείρευε is never romanized).

fix.grammar: Two imperfects = two actions running together: τραγουδούσε όταν μαγείρευε (tragoudoúse ótan mageíreve).

issue: Tip's 'worked example' just repeats the bare phrase ξανά και ξανά a second time — no in-context example showing it with a verb.

fix.grammar: ξανά και ξανά = again and again: έβλεπα ξανά και ξανά (évlepa xaná kai xaná = I watched again and again).

issue: Aspect-gloss mismatch: English 'I went to bed at ten' reads as a one-off event (would be aorist έπεσα), but έπεφτα is habitual imperfect. Learner prompted with this English will produce the aorist. Tip covers only the idiom, not the aspect.

fix.english: I used to go to bed at ten.

issue: Gloss reads as one occasion ('He left the window open all night' = aorist άφησε), but άφηνε is habitual imperfect. Tip signals the habit ('he'd leave it open') but the gloss itself contradicts it.

fix.english: He used to leave the window open all night.

issue: Romanization missing accent: γελούσαμε romanized 'gelousame' — should be geloúsame.

fix.grammar: μαζί της = with her: γελούσαμε μαζί της (geloúsame mazí tis); with him is μαζί του.

issue: Aspect-gloss mismatch: exclamation 'Your mother danced really nicely!' reads as one occasion (aorist χόρεψε), but χόρευε is imperfect (characteristic/habitual). No tip to disambiguate.

fix.english: Your mother used to dance really nicely!

issue: Aspect-gloss mismatch: 'My husband left early for work' most naturally reads as one event (aorist έφυγε), but έφευγε models a routine. No tip to disambiguate; learner will produce the aorist from this prompt.

fix.english: My husband used to leave early for work.

issue: Tip's worked example (ήμασταν φίλοι με τον Γιάννη) has no romanization — required for non-Latin script.

fix.grammar: Greek says 'we were friends with Yiannis': ήμασταν φίλοι με τον Γιάννη (ímastan fíloi me ton Giánni).

issue: Tip has no romanization for either Greek form (έτρωγα, τηλεφώνησες).

fix.grammar: έτρωγα (étroga = I was eating, ongoing); τηλεφώνησες (tilefónises = you called, one moment).

issue: Tip has no romanization for πήγαινα or έκλεισε.

fix.grammar: πήγαινα (pígaina = I used to go, habit); έκλεισε (ékleise = it closed, once and for good).

issue: Tip has no romanization for the worked example ήθελα, αλλά δεν μπόρεσα.

fix.grammar: Wanting is a state, managing is one-off: ήθελα, αλλά δεν μπόρεσα (íthela, allá den bóresa).

issue: Tip has no romanization for περίμενα.

fix.grammar: περίμενα (perímena) covers both pasts of περιμένω — context says if it's 'waited' or 'was waiting'.
